tongatapu-21.text: built in the 13th century by King Tuʻitātui for his two sons (bio variant 1)
tongatapu-21.source: Wikipedia says 13th c.; Tonga Tourism says 11th century AD; Wikivoyage 'around 1200 AD'
tongatapu-21.fix: Sources conflict on the century. Use: 'Coral limestone trilithon at Niutōua, said to have been raised by a king for his two sons.' (Wikivoyage also calls the son theory one of several, so keep 'said to').

tongatapu-21.text: nicknamed the Stonehenge of the Pacific
in Niutōua village, on Tongatapu's eastern side

tongatapu-21.fix: Wikivoyage lists hours 09:00-18:00 but no price; no fee found. Treat 'open' with caution: hours suggest a managed site, so 'entry' basis with free:true is safer than 'open'.

tongatapu-26.text: price TOP 20 per person, costBasis entry
tongatapu-26.source: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tongatapu (Anahulu Caves listing, updated Aug 2024: 'T$20 per person'); operator pages (home, tour.html, beach.html) show no price

tongatapu-27.text: daily produce market; produce on ground floor, handicrafts upstairs
tongatapu-27.source: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tongatapu; https://www.tongatourism.travel/our-islands/tongatapu (Talamahu market sells fresh tropical produce and Tongan arts and crafts)
tongatapu-27.fix: 'Daily' and the floor split are Wikivoyage's reading; if unsure drop 'daily'.

tongatapu-28.text: a wreck to snorkel / snorkel gear to hire
tongatapu-28.fix: Transient: the wreck is an old half-sunken/upturned ship that is rusting and sharp, not a permanent sight. Remove the wreck: 'Small island 10 minutes by boat from Nukuʻalofa, with beaches, a restaurant and snorkel gear to hire.' Draft 3 has no wreck and is safe.

No island day-access fee appears in any source (Wikivoyage gives only boat T$20 return and overnight accommodation rates). Sources are silent, not explicit, so treat as unconfirmed; boat fare must not be the price. Keep free:true. Note Wikivoyage's T$20 return fare differs from nothing else in sources.
